pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

+// Each person's part of an amount in cents, as [name, cents] pairs in the order of people. When the amount does

1	// HTTP entry point: finds the route, reads the JSON body of the routes that take one, runs the handler and
     2	// saves the store after every change. Env: PORT (default 3000), DATA_FILE (default groups.json).
     3	import { existsSync } from 'node:fs'
     4	import { createServer } from 'node:http'
     5	import { dirname, resolve } from 'node:path'
     6	import { errorReply, parseJsonObject, readBody, send } from './lib/http.mjs'
     7	import { findRoute } from './lib/routes.mjs'
     8	import { load, save } from './lib/store.mjs'
     9	
    10	const DEFAULT_PORT = 3000
    11	const MAX_PORT = 65535
    12	
    13	// Builds the server around the store in dataFile. The store is kept in memory; each change is saved before it
    14	// replaces the in-memory copy, so a failed save changes nothing.
    15	export function createApp(dataFile) {
    16	  let state = load(dataFile)
    17	  return createServer(async (req, res) => {
    18	    try {
    19	      // Prefixing the origin keeps a request path like //host/groups a path, not a host.
    20	      const url = new URL(`http://localhost${req.url}`)
    21	      const route = findRoute(req.method, url.pathname)
    22	      if (!route) return send(res, { status: 404, body: { error: 'not found' } })
    23	      const body = route.takesBody ? parseJsonObject(await readBody(req)) : undefined
    24	      const reply = route.handler({ state, params: route.params, query: url.searchParams, body })
    25	      if (reply.state) {
    26	        save(dataFile, reply.state)
    27	        state = reply.state
    28	      }
    29	      send(res, reply)
    30	    } catch (err) {
    31	      send(res, errorReply(err))
    32	    }
    33	  })
    34	}
    35	
    36	function fail(message) {
    37	  console.error(`cannot start: ${message}`)
    38	  process.exitCode = 1
    39	}
    40	
    41	// A plain message for the OS errors a bad DATA_FILE gives; any other error keeps its own.
    42	function loadErrorMessage(err, file) {
    43	  if (err.code === 'EISDIR') return `DATA_FILE ${file} is a folder, not a file`
    44	  if (err.code === 'EACCES') return `cannot read DATA_FILE ${file}: permission denied`
    45	  return err.message
    46	}
    47	
    48	function main() {
    49	  const port = Number(process.env.PORT || DEFAULT_PORT)
    50	  if (!Number.isInteger(port) || port < 0 || port > MAX_PORT) {
    51	    return fail(`PORT must be a whole number from 0 to ${MAX_PORT}, got "${process.env.PORT}"`)
    52	  }
    53	  const file = process.env.DATA_FILE || 'groups.json'
    54	  // Without this check the server would start, then answer 500 to every change it cannot save.
    55	  if (!existsSync(dirname(resolve(file)))) return fail(`folder for DATA_FILE ${file} does not exist`)
    56	  let server
    57	  try {
    58	    server = createApp(file)
    59	  } catch (err) {
    60	    return fail(loadErrorMessage(err, file))
    61	  }
    62	  server.on('error', err => fail(err.message))
    63	  server.listen(port, '127.0.0.1', () => {
    64	    console.log(`listening on http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}`)
    65	  })
    66	}
    67	
    68	if (import.meta.main) main()

content.text:
I found no spec violations in `POST /groups/:id/import` or in the two bug fixes, so this is a pass at 9/10. The fixes listed below are small readability points, not correctness problems.

The existing tests pass (39 of 39). I couldn't run my own edge-case script because the Bash call was denied. So I checked those cases by reading the code against the README, including `' taxi '` against a recorded `Taxi`, `'TAXI'` later in the same import, `null`, `[]`, `{type:'x'}`, a payment with `description`, Ann paying Ann, and amount 0. I did not grade `test/`.

**Spec conformance** (`/root/bench-runs/h5-a85f2060/lib/import.mjs`):
- **Check order:** 413 and the "body is a JSON object" check happen in `server.mjs`/`http.mjs`. Then comes 404, then the 400 messages in the README's order. The first unknown body field is found in `Object.keys` order. `dry_run`/`skip_recorded` are false only when the key is absent (`Object.hasOwn`), so `null` gets the "must be true or false" 400.
- **Rule order per entry:** `not-an-object` (covers `null` and arrays), then `bad-type`, `unknown-field`, then each field in order. Payments check `bad-from`, then `bad-to` (including from equal to to), then `bad-amount`. `split: null` is present, so it is checked and gives `bad-split`.
- **Duplicate and already-recorded:** every entry that passes the field rules goes into `seen` before its own result is decided. So an earlier entry still counts for `duplicate` when it was itself `duplicate`, `already-recorded` or skipped. `duplicate` is checked before `already-recorded`. Only the group's own expenses count as recorded. Descriptions are compared after `trim().toLowerCase()`, amounts in cents, and `split` is ignored. Payments are never checked for either rule.
- **`skip_recorded`:** only an entry whose first broken rule is `already-recorded` is skipped. `skipped` comes out ascending because entries are handled in order.
- **Ids, dry run and writes:** ids continue each kind's own count in entry order, and skipped entries take none. A dry run returns 200 with no `state`, so the counters don't move. When every entry is skipped, `parsed.length === 0` and nothing is written. Balances come from the new store.

**Bug fixes:**
- `/root/bench-runs/h5-a85f2060/lib/validate.mjs:64` now uses `Math.round` instead of `Math.trunc`. That is safe because the existing two-decimal check already rejects anything that rounding could turn into a wrong value.
- `/root/bench-runs/h5-a85f2060/lib/ledger.mjs:11-13` hands the leftover cents to the first people. That matches the README example (3.34 / 3.33 / 3.33), and balances use the same function, so they still add up to 0.

**Style:** comments follow the same house style as the surrounding files. The README Layout section and the routes table are updated.

## GRADE
Overall: 9/10
Verdict: pass
structure: 9 — clear split into parseBody / parseEntry / review / importEntries and returns a new store, but `return problems.push(...)` uses push's return value to exit the loop early
naming: 8 — names are clear, but parseMember gets placeholder messages ('bad payer', 'bad from', 'bad to') that never reach the user and look like real error text
duplication: 8 — the expense and payment field parsing repeats parseExpense/addPayment from expenses.mjs; acceptable because each field needs its own rule name, but the field order is now kept in two places
size: 10 — new file is 141 lines and the longest function is about 32 lines
errors: 9 — only ValidationError becomes a BrokenRule, other errors are rethrown and errorReply turns them into a 500; 400/422 replies match the spec exactly
tests: n/a — written by another section
security: 10 — body and entry keys are allow-listed, no injection paths, `__proto__` keys are refused as unknown fields
leftovers: 10 — no debug code, commented-out code or TODOs
Fixes:
- /root/bench-runs/h5-a85f2060/lib/import.mjs:98 replace `return problems.push(...)` / `return skipped.push(index)` (also lines 100-101) with a push followed by a plain `return`, or an if/else chain, so the push's return value isn't used to exit early
- /root/bench-runs/h5-a85f2060/lib/import.mjs:66 the 'bad payer' / 'bad from' / 'bad to' messages (also lines 72-73) are never shown; pass the rule name, or a constant with a comment saying the message is unused here
- /root/bench-runs/h5-a85f2060/lib/import.mjs:46 add a one-line comment to parseBody saying it checks the body in the 400 order the spec lists, like its neighbours have
